key_insight: Differentiable digital twins combine atomic-system simulation and gradient-based optimization to improve quantum gate performance in neutral-atom and trapped-ion platforms.
engineering_relevance: The toolset supports hardware-aware gate optimization, calibration, and characterization to address noise and imperfections in atomic quantum processors.
method: Model atomic quantum systems and simulate qubit gate dynamics.
Use automatic differentiation for gradient-based quantum optimal control.
Integrate benchmarking to evaluate gate performance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports detailed neutral-atom and trapped-ion case studies showing improved gate fidelities, but provides no numerical results.
watch_item: Practical gains depend on how accurately the digital twin captures experimental noise and hardware imperfections.
paper_title: Differentiable Digital Twins for Optimization, Calibration, and Characterization of Neutral-Atom- and Ion-based Quantum Computers
